Readings are approximate (around ±30%): the phone lens is not a real lux meter. Bright direct sunlight in view can saturate the sensor. Place phone horizontally, back camera facing straight out the window.
Exposure mode: waiting for the camera…
This phone has NO AE metering-region support: aim the phone slightly to the LEFT, away from dark walls, to prevent AE overexposure.
AE metering: center of frame (dark wall on the right is partly ignored).
Hybrid mode: manual exposure locked - the dark wall does NOT affect the readings (driver verified).

Back camera is opened with pure auto-exposure (CONTROL_AE_MODE_ON, flash off, AE lock off); the app only reads back the exposure the camera chose.
k must be a positive number (typical: 1–10).
No camera reading yet - put the phone in daylight for about 10 seconds, or start logging on the main screen.
Reference lux (from another light meter / app)
No calibration points stored yet. k defaults to the manual value in Settings.

Hold this phone and your reference device side by side, both back cameras facing straight out the window at the same spot. Type the reference lux value and add the point. Add 2–3 points in different light (cloudy, bright, evening) for a better average.
Enter the reference lux as a positive number.
